profile.reading: This is InfreschiLab, a small Italian software development business based in Lentiscosa, a hamlet of the town of Camerota in the province of Salerno, Campania, Italy, run by an individual named Andrea per the operator field on this record. Despite the data center style tagging in source data, and despite a name that might suggest cooling or refrigeration given the Italian word infreschi relates to refreshing or cooling, InfreschiLabs own site describes it as a custom software house building web applications, business management software, Android and iOS mobile apps, and desktop applications, with a portfolio referencing projects dating back to at least 2007, suggesting the business has operated in some form since roughly the mid to late 2000s, though no formal founding date is stated. Named products include Liduz, a cloud management platform for beach clubs, and Hoteluz, hotel property management software, both reflecting the tourism heavy economy of this stretch of the Campanian coast known as the Cilento. This registry found no evidence connecting InfreschiLab to any physical server room or data center infrastructure beyond what appears to be a small, likely home based or small office software development business, and records that honestly rather than fabricating data center specifications for it. Camerota and the surrounding Cilento coast form part of the Cilento, Vallo di Diano e Alburni National Park area in southern Campania, a rural and tourism dependent region where small locally based software developers like InfreschiLab typically serve nearby hospitality and small business clients directly rather than competing in national or international enterprise software markets. The businesss product names, Liduz for beach club operators and Hoteluz for hotels, both play on the Italian word luce, or light, a common naming convention among small Italian software vendors targeting hospitality clients along the countrys coastline.
